# fastf 3.20.0: open work first, and no folder pulled from under what uses it

Nothing about an existing project changes. Every `PROJECT_INFO.md`,
`config.toml` and template works untouched, and a todo's number is what it
always was.

## Open work first

A list where most todos are ticked buried the ones still open. Now each
phase shows its open todos, then folds the done ones into one row:
`✓ 4 done`.

- **In the app's pane**, Enter on that row shows the done ones in place, in
  the file's order, and Enter again hides them. A todo you tick keeps its row
  while you stay on the project, so Enter again is the undo; it joins its
  fold once you move on. `+` on a fold adds an open todo to that phase, just
  above it.
- **`fastf todo list`** prints the same: each phase, its open todos with their
  numbers, and the count of the done ones. `--all` prints every todo, ticked
  ones included, in file order; `--open` leaves the counts out. A script that
  reads `[x]` lines from the default list should ask for `--all`.
- **The file never changes order.** A todo's number is its place in the file,
  so `fastf todo done ID0047 6` means the same todo before and after, whatever
  the list shows first. `fastf show --json` now carries each todo's `number`.
- Piped, `todo list` and `desk --plain` keep to 100 columns (the terminal's
  width on a terminal) instead of padding every line to the longest todo.

## A folder something is using is not moved, renamed or deleted

A move used to go ahead while a container ran from the folder, a dev server
wrote into it or a service named it — and whatever it was kept the old path:
a container makes the folder again, empty, at its next start, and a server
writes into a copy that is about to be removed. Now `fastf move`, `rename`
and `delete`, and the same verbs in the app, look first, and refuse, naming
each thing:

```
error: ID0047 is in use, so it was not moved:
  node (pid 4242) is working in src
  podman (pid 7001) has v2/addon/data mounted at /app/data
  coda.service (enabled, running) names it: WorkingDirectory=/home/user/Projects/…
stop them, then move it again
hint: --force moves it anyway, and the result names what used it: `fastf move ID0047 archive --yes --force`
```

The look reads only what the system says — every process's working folder,
open files, program and arguments, every process's mounts (so a root
container's bind mounts too), and service unit files — and never asks a tool
by name, so a container runtime, a database or a server fastf has never heard
of is seen the same way.

- **What never counts**: fastf, whoever asked (the shell, the agent, the app
  and every process above them) and what the command is piped to or from.
- **Only a note**: a shell sitting at its prompt in the folder, a terminal
  window opened there, a file manager opened on it, a unit that is disabled
  and stopped. The move goes, and says to `cd` or what will show the old
  folder.
- **`--force`** goes past what uses it, says what it went past, and writes
  one line to `fastf.log`. With `--yes` and no `--force`, the command exits 1
  with the list and the command that goes past it — what a script or an agent
  reads. In the app the question's cursor rests on *Cancel*.
- A move that paused waiting for a mount is asked again before it goes on:
  while its folder is in use, `fastf reconcile` leaves it and says so.

What it cannot see: another user's processes show only their arguments and
mounts, so a root container working in a folder it mounted from above the
project is not seen.

## Smaller things

- The static Linux build (the AUR's `fast-folder-bin`) now allocates through
  mimalloc: reading every project — a reindex, a search, the app's reads — no
  longer runs about twice as slow as the glibc build.
- A second Ctrl-C, hang-up or terminate gives the terminal back and exits with
  the signal's own code: 130, 129 or 143.
- A date in the search bar cut by a wide character (`created>2026-01-1€`) no
  longer crashes the app.
- Cancelling a move or a delete while it looks at what uses the folder stops
  it before anything changes.

## The last release for Windows

3.20.0 is the last release with a native Windows build, and it keeps working.
From 4.0.0 fastf is Linux only; on Windows, run it inside WSL.

How it works: [docs/projects.md](https://github.com/cristocola/fast-folder/blob/main/docs/projects.md)
and [docs/app.md](https://github.com/cristocola/fast-folder/blob/main/docs/app.md)
